definition: An attraction between separate molecules; much weaker than a covalent bond, and the force overcome when a molecular substance melts or boils.
The attraction between an instantaneous dipole in one molecule and the dipole it induces in a neighbour; present between all molecules and stronger with more electrons and more surface contact.
The attraction between the permanent dipoles of neighbouring polar molecules, with the $\delta+$ end of one near the $\delta-$ end of the next.

The attraction between a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on a nearby N, O or F atom; usually between molecules, though it can form within a large molecule such as a protein, and it is not a covalent bond.
The umbrella term for London (dispersion), dipole–induced dipole and dipole–dipole forces; it does not include hydrogen bonding.
